messages:
maya: Quick sync — building the token-econ dashboard (cost per 1k + cache/batch savings). Need to lock the canonical signals and join keys from runtime, billing, and telemetry. Who owns what?

liam: I own the runtime side. We can emit per-request: request_id, model, route, tokens_in, tokens_out, kv_cache_hits, kv_cache_misses, batch_size, served_variant. Events now are runtime.request.start / runtime.request.finish and runtime.kv.hit/miss.

oliver: Data infra note: for reliable joins we need a single request_id propagated to billing and observability. If runtime can't, we'll accept (instance_ts, host, seq) but that makes dedupe messy. Can runtime add request_id header?

liam: Yes, we can plumb request_id through. Plan: add request_id to all runtime events and to the exit path sent to billing. Will open a tiny PR.

kevin: Heads-up from routing/quotas: some requests spawn primary+fallback model calls. We shouldn't count both fully — for cost/1k show 'charged_tokens' (what billing billed) and 'compute_attempt_tokens' (all tokens consumed). Otherwise averages will be inflated.

maya: Good call. UX needs both: billed cost and wasted compute. Sasha — for the console, what fields do you expect from the aggregated table?

sasha: For dashboard rows: route, model_version, window_start, window_end, requests, median_latency, billed_tokens, billed_cost_per_1k, compute_tokens, cache_saved_tokens, batch_saved_tokens, fallback_attempts, deduped_requests. We'll surface a stacked bar for savings: cache vs batching vs quantization (if available).

oliver: We should precompute savings on the infra side to avoid heavy GROUP BYs in the console. Proposed materialized view fields: window_ts, route, model, requests, billed_tokens, compute_tokens, cache_saved_tokens, batch_saved_tokens, cost_usd. Then console reads ready-to-plot numbers.

liam: Implementation detail: runtime can calculate per-request cache_saved = prefetch_tokens - served_tokens_when_cache_hit; batch_saved = batch_effect_estimate (we can approximate by (batch_size - 1)*avg_tokens_per_additional_request?). I'll ship an estimator in the agent.

kevin: Also need a schema for 'served_by' to understand routing decisions: primary_model, fallback_model, was_routed_by (policy_id). Adds transparency for rollouts/experiments.

maya: Action items summary: liam add request_id + compute attempt tokens & 'served_by' fields; oliver add materialized view proto + join keys; sasha will mock the panels with sample numbers; kevin to note quota/fallback semantics for billing. I'll collect PR links here. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: New doc: https://redwood-internal/papers/token-econ-signals-v1 (schema + example pipeline). PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/+/3456

oliver: I'll coordinate ETL window (5m vs 1h). Suggest 5m rollups for near-real-time console, 1h for aggregated billing.

maya: Perfect. Let's reconvene after PRs land. If anyone sees edge cases (multi-model fanout, cached reroutes), drop them here.

liam: quick sample telemetry payload (will include request_id):
```json
{
  "event": "runtime.request.finish",
  "request_id": "req_01F8XQ2Z",
  "model": "rw-13b-v2",
  "route": "chat.completions",
  "tokens_in": 42,
  "tokens_out": 328,
  "kv_cache_hits": 1,
  "kv_cache_misses": 0,
  "batch_size": 3,
  "compute_attempt_tokens": 328,
  "billed_tokens": 328,
  "served_by": ["primary:rw-13b-v2"]
}
```

sasha: That payload is perfect for mocks. I'll add a panel that computes billed_cost_per_1k = billed_tokens / 1000 * price_per_1k (from pricing table).

kevin: One more: include 'is_deduped' flag when a request was suppressed by cache dedupe upstream, so ETL can decide whether to count it as a request for quotas.

maya: Thanks everyone — I'll track the PRs and schedule a 20m follow-up on Friday.
